title: Same-height projectile velocity comparison on rising and falling branches

authority_basis.claim_scope: Repository-backed SBA04 atom compares equal-height rising/falling states: same vx, equal |vy|, opposite vy signs and equal speed but different velocity vectors.

concepts.statement: For the standard projectile model, rising and falling states at the same vertical height have the same horizontal component and equal vertical-component magnitude with opposite signs, so their speeds match while their velocity vectors differ.
concepts.why_required: Equal height creates a state relation that distinguishes scalar speed symmetry from vector velocity direction.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Equal speed may be incorrectly upgraded to equal velocity or the falling sign of vy may be lost.

symbols.name: vertical component at falling same-height state
vertical component at rising same-height state

conditions: Same vertical height relative to one origin

model_conditions.condition: The compared states belong to the same no-drag projectile, use the same height origin, and occur under uniform gravity.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The equal-magnitude/opposite-sign vertical-component relation is a symmetry of the standard conservative projectile model.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Drag or a different force model can break same-height speed symmetry.

representations.semantic_geometry: Two marked points at one horizontal height line on the rising and falling branches show equal vx arrows, equal-magnitude opposite vy arrows and equal-length resultant velocity arrows with different directions.
must_not_imply: same height means same velocity vector
representations.verification_method: Compare component pairs: vx must match, vy must reverse sign with equal magnitude, and reconstructed speed magnitudes must match.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify the rising and falling states at the same declared vertical height.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: States at different heights may be compared as if symmetry applied.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Compare components: keep vx unchanged and reverse the sign of vy while preserving its magnitude.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Equal speed may be confused with equal velocity.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Reconstruct the speed magnitudes and distinguish equal scalar speed from different vector direction.

required_transformations.description: Translate equal-height geometry into component symmetry and then into the distinction between equal speed and unequal velocity vectors.
Use the same-height component symmetry to solve scalar-versus-vector comparison questions, preserve the vertical sign reversal, and verify that equal speed does not imply equal velocity.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: At the same height the projectile has the same velocity vector on the way up and on the way down.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The speeds match and the two states occupy the same vertical level.
trigger_contexts: launch and landing at same height
misconceptions.required_counterexample: The rising state has vy>0 while the falling state has vy<0 even though their speed magnitudes match.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Display the two velocity arrows at equal height with mirrored vertical components.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Keep vx the same but reverse vy; equal component squares produce equal speed but not equal vector direction.
misconceptions.verification: Write the two component pairs and check they are not identical vectors.

problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the two velocity component pairs before comparing magnitudes or directions.
